text:
maya: kicking off a cross-run benchmark writeup for embed/rerank. goal: apples-to-apples kernel sweep + batching grid + kv warm/cold tails. link to sheet: https://tiny.redwood/bench-stressgrid :point_right:

sam: awesome. can you include both replay and synthetic traffic patterns? last time replay hid some tail spikes.

maya: yes — plan is to run replay harness (prod trace subset) + synthetic stressgrid (controlled qps/batch dims). stressgrid will iterate: batch sizes [1,4,8,16,32,64], dims [128,256,512,1024], payload sizes [1,4,16 docs], kv state [cold,warm,partial] and kernels [fused-attn,flash,default].

cheng: remind me: how are we modeling kv partial? random fraction of cached prefixes?

maya: partial = 50% queries hit existing KV entries pre-warmed. we do 0%, 50%, 100%. also run a "kv-warmup" pass to simulate steady-state.

eli: quick profiling note: in earlier runs the kernel selector favored flash for 512/1 but fused-attn had better tail at high concurrency. I dumped perf counters — attaching snippet:

```
# perf output sample
model: embedder-v2
batch: 32 dims:512
kernel: flash
latency_p50: 12.3ms
latency_p95: 92.1ms
latency_p99: 210.7ms
dispatch_stalls: 4.2%
kv_miss_rate: 48%
```

sam: interesting. did you capture per-request kernel decisions? we might be switching mid-batch when lengths vary. that could explain spikes.

eli: yes — selector logs included. we saw ~8% mid-batch fallback to default kernel when sequence length > threshold. sequence lengths in rerank are uneven (some docs long).

maya: action: add a histogram of seq-len per batch to the dashboard. also add a stress scenario where we craft long doc tails to force fallback.

perf-bot: automated run 1757772000 completed: replay-run qps=1200, avg_batch=12, p99=180ms, p99.9=420ms (cold kv) — full CSV uploaded to /perf/runs/1757772000.csv

sam: noted. p99.9 420ms cold kv is too high for the Dedicated SLA. can we test adaptive batching (cap batch size when kv_miss>30%)? previous simulations suggested ~20% reduction in p99.9 with adaptive cap.

cheng: we should also sanity-check embedding dim scaling. embedding ops are O(dim) and memory footprint affects kernel choice. propose microbench: single-threaded kernel-only run sweeping dims and reporting throughput and L2 cache miss rate.

maya: good call. add microbench in plan. also iterate quantized kernels (int8) for dims 512+ and capture quality/regression with our eval set.

eli: one weird regression from yesterday: after kernel-switch patch, qps dropped ~6% for dims=1024 with batch>64. suspect scheduling jitter in our batcher. I have traces showing <200us scheduling jitter normally, now spikes to 1.2ms under load.

maya: mark that as a regression to triage. @sam can you take the batcher traces?

sam: on it. I'll compare pre/post kernel-switch traces and run the same stressgrid with disabled kernel-switch to isolate.

perf-bot: NOTE: baseline stressgrid config committed at rev a1b2c3. stressgrid yaml snippet:

```
stressgrid:
  qps: [200,600,1200]
  batch_sizes: [1,4,8,16,32,64]
  dims: [128,256,512,1024]
  payloads: [1,4,16]
  kv_modes: [cold,partial,warm]
  kernels: [default,flash,fused-attn,int8]
```

maya: final asks before we run full matrix: 1) add seq-len histogram, 2) microbench for dim scaling, 3) rerun with adaptive batching policy toggle, 4) collect kernel-selection per-request, 5) store perf counters + flamegraphs.

cheng: I'll own the seq-len hist and microbench.

sam: I'll handle batcher traces and adaptive policy experiment.

eli: I'll re-run the failing 1024 batch>64 case and upload traces + perf counter dumps.

maya: thanks — let's reconvene tomorrow after initial sweep. :thumbsup:

sam: bumping this — starting replay run now (replay subset 2026-03-prod). will post results in thread.

perf-bot: run 1757774000 finished: synthetic stressgrid qps=600, dim=512, batch=32, kv=partial => p50 14ms p95 110ms p99 230ms p99.99 890ms (observed kernel mid-batch fallbacks ~6%). CSV: /perf/runs/1757774000.csv

maya: thanks, that's helpful. we'll iterate on adaptive cap and re-evaluate.
